papers.title: Parsing the Pediatric Mood Spectrum in U.S. Youth: Transdiagnostic Severity Versus Phenotypic Specificity
papers.abstract: Objective: Emotion dysregulation and irritability occur across pediatric disorders, complicating distinctions between general symptom burden and specific clinical presentations. Person-centered analyses can look at profiles of scores to identify groups with similar presentations. We examined whether modeling shared and domain-specific symptom variance identified differentiated profiles in youth. Method: Caregivers of 2,187 US youth ages 6-18 completed 87 items assessing emotion dysregulation, depression, mania-related symptoms, sleep-related impairment, and attention and behavioral problems. An ordinal bifactor model estimated one general and 13 specific factors. Latent profile analyses used standardized scores on all 14 factors, with an expanded raw-score analysis as a comparator. We examined caregiver-reported diagnoses and functioning and approximately two-week classification agreement among 166 recontacted caregivers. Results: The general factor accounted for 62% of common variance ({omega}H=.94), although model fit was mixed (CFI=.884; RMSEA=.058; SRMR=.092). A provisional four-class solution distinguished population-modal (67.4%), internalizing (11.8%), attention/hyperactivity (11.0%), and unusual-thought/elevated-mood (9.8%) profiles. Entropy was .83, but model enumeration and initialization checks did not establish a unique solution. Profiles showed overlapping diagnostic and functional correlates. Recontact agreement was 78.9% ({kappa}=.60). Irritability-specific reliability was limited, constraining interpretation of its weak profile differentiation. Conclusions: General symptom burden coexisted with differentiated residual symptom patterns. These findings support evaluating severity alongside symptom configuration, without equating profiles with diagnoses or weak residual irritability signals with limited clinical relevance. Measurement refinement, model-selection verification, and confirmation of classification-error-adjusted associations are needed before clinical application, but profiles could simplify clinical interpretation of sets of scales.

papers.title: Real-time wearable detection of respiratory infections in pediatric transplant households
papers.abstract: Consumer-grade wearables can continuously and longitudinally measure health signals such as heart rate (HR), activity, and sleep. While changes in these signals have been implicated in the early detection of infection (e.g., influenza, SARS-CoV-2) and real-time alerting systems have been developed, evidence from prospective deployment in pediatric transplant households remains limited. Here, we study the application of a resting heart rate (RHR)-based real-time alerting algorithm to detect respiratory virus infection in a cohort of solid organ transplant recipients and their household members (n=146) in a Phase IV clinical trial (NCT06161454). Reliable and efficient alerting for infection events may be particularly relevant for this population, enabling isolation, clinical management, and/or treatment. Of 31 antigen-test outcomes, nearly all (29/31, 93.5%) correspond to either influenza, COVID, or other patient-reported symptoms. We describe RHR, HR, activity, and sleep/circadian rhythm features around clinical alarm events, identifying candidate features for further investigation and algorithm improvement.

papers.title: Attenuated alpha state transitions and disrupted repetition-dependent temporal adaptation in mild cognitive impairment
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) may involve impaired dynamic regulation of brain states that is not captured by conventional resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). We quantified occipital alpha (8-12 Hz) transitions during three repeated eye-opening/eye-closure cycles in 60 healthy controls (HC) and 77 participants with MCI. Eye-state events were refined from frontal ocular artifacts. Transition magnitude was measured by the log-transformed post-/pre-event energy ratio, and transition success by the expected direction of alpha change. For canonical transitions meeting prespecified fit-quality criteria, mono-exponential fitting yielded transition onset (t_onset) and the post-onset time constant (tau). MCI showed weaker alpha suppression during eye opening, weaker alpha enhancement during eye closure, and lower odds of transition success. No significant group difference in tau was detected within the canonical quality-controlled subset. In contrast, t_onset showed significant Group x Trial interactions in both conditions: HC developed later onset during eye opening and earlier onset during eye closure across repetitions, whereas MCI showed no comparable change. These findings suggest reduced alpha state-transition capacity and altered repetition-dependent temporal organization in MCI.

papers.title: Longitudinal Pain Profiles and Their Clinical and Genetic Correlates in 624,996 U.S. Veterans
papers.abstract: Importance: Pain varies in its intensity and course, yet much of our understanding of pain is based on cross-sectional assessments or longitudinal studies of selected clinical populations. Routinely collected electronic health record data may enable characterization of longitudinal pain patterns at scale. Objective: To identify longitudinal pain profiles among U.S. Veterans and characterize their clinical and polygenic correlates. Design: Cohort study using electronic health record and genomic data from the Million Veteran Program, with up to 16 years of pain assessments collected between 2000 to 2025. Setting: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs health care system. Participants: Million Veteran Program participants assigned to African-like, Admixed American-like, East Asian-like, European-like, or South Asian-like genetically inferred ancestry groups who have at least three years of outpatient numeric rating scale pain records. Exposures: Outpatient pain ratings and polygenic scores for psychiatric, sleep, and substance use traits. Main Outcomes and Measures: Pain profiles were identified using Gaussian finite mixture modeling of pain intensity, directional change, and within-person variability. Profiles were characterized by pain, psychiatric and substance use diagnoses, opioid exposure, body mass index, and polygenic scores. Results: Among 624,996 participants (Mean [SD] age at first pain rating=53.4 [13.5] years; 568,833 [91.0%] male), 51,731,567 outpatient pain ratings were analyzed. Three profiles were identified: stable no pain, stable mild pain, and mild-to-moderate increasing pain. Compared with the stable no pain profile, the increasing pain profile had higher odds of chronic pain (OR=21.14 [95% CI: 18.96-23.57]), opioid use disorder (OR=9.32 [95% CI: 8.31-10.45]), opioid exposure (OR=8.61 [95% CI: 8.41-8.83]), major depressive disorder (OR=3.77 [95% CI: 3.67-3.87]), and posttraumatic stress disorder (OR=3.72 [95% CI: 3.61-3.84]). Associations were attenuated but remained after adjustment for mean pain severity. Polygenic scores for depression, insomnia, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and tobacco use disorder were the most consistent predictors of increasing pain across the three largest genetically inferred ancestry groups. Conclusions and Relevance: Longitudinal modeling of routinely collected pain scores identified pain profiles associated with clinical burden and polygenic liability. These profiles captured clinically meaningful information beyond mean pain severity alone, highlighting the value of longitudinal pain phenotyping in electronic health record data.

papers.title: AI chatbots abandon sleep apnoea referral when simulated patients minimise symptoms
papers.abstract: Background: Patients increasingly consult free artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots about their symptoms, but these models may favour agreement with the patient over accuracy. In obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), where most cases in the general population remain undiagnosed and diagnosis depends on referral, this could validate symptom denial. We tested whether consumer chatbots maintain guideline-concordant referral when a simulated patient minimises symptoms. Methods: Seven guideline-concordant and standardised OSA vignettes (apnoea-hypopnoea-index, AHI 8-52 events/h; body mass index 28-42 kg/m2) were presented to five free chatbots (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash and Grok-4.3) under neutral and symptom-minimising conditions (10 simulated conversations per model-vignette-condition cell; N=700). Referral maintenance was scored by a structured rubric and every capitulation was human-confirmed. Results: All chatbots maintained referral recommendations in neutral conversations (350/350; 100%). When simulated patients minimised symptoms and resisted referral, maintenance fell to 64.3% (225/350), a reduction of 35.7 percentage points (95% CI 5.5-66.0; p=0.028). Rates ranged from 55.7% to 85.7% across chatbots, but evidence of between-chatbot differences was inconsistent across analyses. Rates differed across clinical vignettes (p=0.001). A variance analysis estimated greater variation between vignettes than between chatbots. In the three driving-risk vignettes, referral recommendations were abandoned in 46-68% of symptom-minimising conversations, pooling all five chatbots within each vignette. Conclusions: Consumer AI chatbots abandoned correct OSA referral recommendations in about one-third of symptom-minimising conversations, with higher observed abandonment in simulated cases involving driving risk. This may delay appropriate assessment and raises patient- and public-safety concerns.

papers.title: Atrial fibrillation begets atrial fibrillation - serum-driven amplification of atrial electrical instability
papers.abstract: Rationale: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is sustained by electrical triggers and atrial substrate, but whether AF itself generates circulating factors that acutely reinforce arrhythmogenesis is unknown. Objective: To determine whether rhythm-dependent serum bioactivity directly destabilizes atrial electrophysiology and to identify associated cellular mechanisms and circulating mediators. Methods and Results: Cardiac samples were obtained from patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) during AF and after restoration of sinus rhythm (SR) using electrical cardioversion. In isolated Langendorff-perfused mouse hearts, AF serum increased the duration, frequency, and cumulative burden of spontaneous atrial depolarizations compared with paired control perfusate. In human induced pluripotent stem cell derived atrial cardiomyocytes, AF patient serum decreased Ca2-transient amplitudes without significant effect on kinetics or Ca2 spark activity. Moreover, AF serum reduced peak sodium current without materially altering voltage-dependent gating or paced action-potential properties. Data-independent acquisition proteomics identified rhythm-associated changes in extracellular-matrix, proteolytic, inflammatory, and signaling proteins, including MMP9, Ccathepsin G, and 14-3-3 family members. Targeted pathway perturbation differentially modified serum-induced Ca2 phenotypes, indicating context-dependent, multifactorial bioactivity. Serum-induced Ca2 responses were not associated with indices of atrial disease severity, including low-voltage substrate burden and left atrial pressure. Conclusions: Persistent AF is accompanied by rhythm-dependent circulating bioactivity that acutely promotes atrial electrical instability and Ca2-dependent trigger formation. These findings extend the concept that AF begets AF beyond tissue-intrinsic remodeling and identify a potentially reversible serum-mediated feed-forward mechanism linking rhythm status and circulating proteomic signals in an atrial substrate severity independent fashion. Keywords: atrial fibrillation; serum; atrial cardiomyopathy; calcium signaling; circulating factors; proteomics

papers.title: Discrete cortico-hippocampal circuit states underlie mood state transitions in depression
papers.abstract: The hippocampus has long been implicated in depression, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Leveraging precision functional mapping in densely sampled individuals and large cross-sectional cohorts, and validating key results in direct intracranial EEG recordings from the human brain, we show that hippocampal connectivity alternates between two discrete and opposing network states on the order of minutes: one dominated by default mode network (DMN) coupling and another by sensorimotor system (SM) coupling. This dynamic switching is a fundamental property of hippocampal function in both healthy brains and in major depressive disorder (MDD). In MDD, this equilibrium is disrupted, such that the DMN-dominant state is overrepresented. In densely sampled individuals, hippocampus-DMN coupling tracks symptom fluctuations over time and normalizes after electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), which drives switches in hippocampal connectivity away from the DMN-dominant state and toward the SM-dominant state, an effect that was closely linked to a positive treatment response. Direct intracranial recordings in patients with MDD identified analogous fluctuations in hippocampal-DMN theta synchrony, which tracks symptom fluctuations over hours and days. Together, these findings identify a dynamic cortico-hippocampal mechanism underlying depression and indicate that successful neuromodulation treatments such as ECT act in part by restoring a dynamic equilibrium in hippocampal network connectivity.

papers.title: Predictors of Activity and Concentration Interference in Adults with Migraine: An Ecological Momentary Assessment Study
papers.abstract: Objective: To identify demographic and daily cognitive, affective, and contextual predictors of headache-related interference with activity and concentration in a smartphone-based migraine cohort, using statistical models appropriate to the ordinal structure of patient-reported interference. Background: Migraine burden extends beyond headache to encompass cognitive and affective disturbance, yet most disability instruments summarize functioning retrospectively and cannot capture day-to-day variability in interference. Ecological momentary assessment addresses this limitation, yet few studies have examined cognitive and affective correlates of interference independent of pain intensity or have modeled interference using methods that respect its ordinal, non-equal-interval structure. Methods: From May 2025 to April 2026, adult participants were enrolled in this prospective, decentralized observational study via specialty clinics and social media campaigns. Eligibility required fulfilling ICHD-3 diagnostic criteria for migraine using a validated electronic survey and experiencing between 3 and 20 monthly headache days. Enrolled individuals recorded daily smartphone diary entries and performed three brief cognitive tests over a 30-day monitoring period. Daily interference with activities and concentration were captured on 5-point ordinal scales and analyzed via cumulative link mixed-effects models incorporating participant-specific random intercepts. Predictor selection across nested specifications relied on likelihood ratio testing and Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) metrics, prioritizing the more parsimonious model when goodness-of-fit was comparable. Results: The analytic sample comprised 1,267 headache-day observations from 143 participants. In the final models, brain fog (OR = 2.49 for activity, 3.19 for concentration), forgetfulness (OR = 1.48, 1.65), and mood disturbance (OR = 1.19, 1.31) were each independently associated with both outcomes (all p < 0.01), while age, sex, and employment status showed no significant association with either. Sleep quality (OR = 0.86) and anticipated next-day enjoyment (OR = 0.81) provided additional explanatory value for activity interference (p < 0.05) but not for concentration interference, for which the three-predictor model of brain fog, forgetfulness, and mood alone was retained as the most parsimonious final model. Conclusions: Cognitive and affective symptoms, rather than demographic or socioeconomic characteristics, are the primary correlates of headache-related functional interference in this cohort. Activity and concentration interference are explained by partially distinct sets of daily influences, supporting the clinical value of assessing cognitive and affective symptoms alongside conventional pain-focused evaluation.

papers.title: NESTApp: A GUI-Based MATLAB Application for Auditable TMS-EEG Preprocessing with EEGLAB
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) preprocessing determines signal quality and interpretation, particularly for transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with EEG (TMS-EEG), where recordings are affected by large and complex stimulation-related artifacts. Several preprocessing approaches have been developed, but substantial variability remains in how pipelines are implemented, documented, and evaluated across recordings, limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies. We developed NESTApp, a MATLAB-based graphical interface built on EEGLAB, to provide an accessible and reproducible framework for implementing and evaluating TMS-EEG preprocessing pipelines. Rather than prescribing a specific pipeline, NESTApp allows users to construct and consistently apply customisable workflows incorporating established EEGLAB and TMS-EEG processing tools, while automatically documenting processing decisions and parameters. Integrated quality-control procedures track data removal and flag recordings based on user-defined criteria, facilitating systematic evaluation across participants. The application also supports group-level visualisation and export of processed TMS-EEG measures for subsequent analyses. Applied to 29 recordings from 16 participants, NESTApp processed 27 and identified those requiring further inspection. By integrating pipeline implementation, documentation, quality control, and group-level evaluation within a single interface, NESTApp provides a transparent framework for TMS-EEG preprocessing that may improve reproducibility, facilitate consistent processing across cohorts, and lower technical barriers to the implementation of established preprocessing approaches.
